items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, who said: One day, Abu Abdillah (a.s) said to me: “O Hammad, do you know how to perform prayer properly?” I said: “O my master, I have memorized the book of Hariz regarding prayer.” Imam (a.s) said: “It does not matter, O Hammad. Stand and pray.” So I stood before Him (a.s), facing the qiblah. I began the prayer, bowed, and prostrated. Then Imam (a.s) said: “O Hammad, you do not perform prayer properly. How unbecoming it is for a man like you, sixty or seventy years may pass over him, and he does not establish even one prayer with all of its boundaries complete?!” Hammad said: ‘So I felt humiliated within myself and I said; “May I be your ransom, then teach me the prayer.” So Abu Abdillah (a.s) stood, facing the qiblah, upright. He (a.s) placed both his hands on his thighs, brought his fingers together, and positioned his feet close together until the distance between them was about the width of three spread-out fingers. He (a.s) pointed all the toes of his feet toward the qiblah, not turning them away from the qiblah, and Imam (a.s) said with humility: “Allahu Akbar.” Then He (a.s) recited al-Hamd with measured tone and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, then paused for a short moment, the amount of time one takes a breath, while standing. Then He (a.s) raised his hands in line with his face and said: “Allahu Akbar,” while still standing. Then He (a.s) bowed and filled his hands with his knees, spreading his fingers apart. He (a.s) pulled his knees backward and straightened his back until, had a drop of water or oil been poured on it, it would not have moved, due to the straightness of his back. He (a.s) extended his neck and closed his eyes. Then Imam (a.s) said tasbih three times with measured tone, saying: ‘Subhana Rabbi al-‘Azim wa bi-hamdih.’ Then He (a.s) stood up straight, and when He (a.s) became fully upright, Imam (a.s) said “‘Samia’a Allahu liman hamidah’ (Allah (swt) has heard the one who praises Him),” then Imam (a.s) said ‘Allahu Akbar’ while standing, and raised his hands in line with his face. Then He (a.s) went into prostration and placed his palms, with fingers joined together, between his knees, in line with his face, and said: ‘Subhana Rabbi al-A’la wa bi-hamdih’ three times. He (a.s) did not rest any part of his body on another part. He (a.s) prostrated on eight bones; the two palms, the two knees, the tips of the big toes, the forehead, and the nose. Imam (a.s) said: “Seven of them are obligatory to prostrate upon, and they are the ones Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in His Book, where He (swt) said: ‘And that the masajid belong to Allah (swt), so do not call upon anyone with Allah (swt)’ (Surah Jinn 72:18). These are the forehead, the two palms, the two knees, and the two big toes. Placing the nose on the ground is a sunnah.” Then He (a.s) raised his head from prostration, and when He (a.s) was fully upright sitting, Imam (a.s) said: ‘Allahu Akbar’. Then He (a.s) sat on his left thigh, placing his right foot on the instep of his left foot, and said: “Astaghfirullaha Rabbi wa atubu ilayh.” Then Imam (a.s) said takbir while sitting and performed the second prostration, saying as Imam (a.s) said in the first. He (a.s) did not rest any part of his body upon another in bowing or in prostration. He (a.s) was balanced and did not place his forearms on the ground. He (a.s) prayed two rak’ahs in this manner, with his fingers joined together, and He (a.s) was seated during the tashahhud. When He (a.s) completed the tashahhud, He (a.s) gave salam and said: ‘O Hammad, pray like this.’”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَوْماً «يَا حَمَّادُ تُحْسِنُ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ» قَالَ فَقُلْتُ يَا سَيِّدِي أَنَا أَحْفَظُ كِتَابَ حَرِيزٍ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« لاَ عَلَيْكَ يَا حَمَّادُ قُمْ فَصَلِّ» قَالَ فَقُمْتُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مُتَوَجِّهاً إِلَى اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَاسْتَفْتَحْتُ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَرَكَعْتُ وَ سَجَدْتُ فَقَالَ« يَا حَمَّادُ لاَ تُحْسِنُ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ مَا أَقْبَحَ بِالرَّجُلِ مِنْكُمْ يَأْتِي عَلَيْهِ سِتُّونَ سَنَةً أَوْ سَبْعُونَ سَنَةً فَلاَ يُقِيمُ صَلاَةً وَاحِدَةً بِحُدُودِهَا تَامَّةً» قَالَ حَمَّادٌ فَأَصَابَنِي فِي نَفْسِي اَلذُّلُّ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ فَعَلِّمْنِي اَلصَّلاَةَ فَقَامَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مُسْتَقْبِلَ اَلْقِبْلَةِ مُنْتَصِباً فَأَرْسَلَ يَدَيْهِ جَمِيعاً عَلَى فَخِذَيْهِ قَدْ ضَمَّ أَصَابِعَهُ وَ قَرَّبَ بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْهِ حَتَّى كَانَ بَيْنَهُمَا قَدْرُ ثَلاَثِ أَصَابِعَ مُنْفَرِجَاتٍ وَ اِسْتَقْبَلَ بِأَصَابِعِ رِجْلَيْهِ جَمِيعاً اَلْقِبْلَةَ لَمْ يُحَرِّفْهَا عَنِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ وَقَالَ بِخُشُوعٍ« اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ» ثُمَّ قَرَأَ اَلْحَمْدَ بِتَرْتِيلٍ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» ثُمَّ صَبَرَ هُنَيْئَةً بِقَدْرِ مَا يَتَنَفَّسُ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ ثُمَّ رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ حِيَالَ وَجْهِهِ وَ قَالَ «اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ» وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ ثُمَّ رَكَعَ وَ مَلَأَ كَفَّيْهِ مِنْ رُكْبَتَيْهِ مُنْفَرِجَاتٍ وَ رَدَّ رُكْبَتَيْهِ إِلَى خَلْفِهِ ثُمَّ اِسْتَوَى ظَهْرُهُ حَتَّى لَوْ صُبَّ عَلَيْهِ قَطْرَةٌ مِنْ مَاءٍ أَوْ دُهْنٍ لَمْ تَزُلْ لاِسْتِوَاءِ ظَهْرِهِ وَمَدَّ عُنُقَهُ وَغَمَّضَ عَيْنَيْهِ ثُمَّ سَبَّحَ ثَلاَثاً بِتَرْتِيلٍ فَقَالَ «سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ اَلْعَظِيمِ وَ بِحَمْدِهِ» ثُمَّ اِسْتَوَى قَائِماً فَلَمَّا اِسْتَمْكَنَ مِنَ اَلْقِيَامِ قَالَ« سَمِعَ اَللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ» ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ وَ رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ حِيَالَ وَجْهِهِ ثُمَّ سَجَدَ وَ بَسَطَ كَفَّيْهِ مَضْمُومَتَيِ اَلْأَصَابِعِ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رُكْبَتَيْهِ حِيَالَ وَجْهِهِ فَقَالَ« سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ اَلْأَعْلَى وَ بِحَمْدِهِ» ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ وَ لَمْ يَضَعْ شَيْئاً مِنْ جَسَدِهِ عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ وَ سَجَدَ عَلَى ثَمَانِيَةِ أَعْظُمٍ اَلْكَفَّيْنِ وَ اَلرُّكْبَتَيْنِ وَ أَنَامِلِ إِبْهَامَيِ اَلرِّجْلَيْنِ وَ اَلْجَبْهَةِ وَ اَلْأَنْفِ وَ قَالَ« سَبْعٌ مِنْهَا فَرْضٌ يُسْجَدُ عَلَيْهَا وَ هِيَ اَلَّتِي ذَكَرَهَا اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فِي كِتَابِهِ وَ قَالَ« وَ أَنَّ اَلْمَسٰاجِدَ لِلّٰهِ فَلاٰ تَدْعُوا مَعَ اَللّٰهِ أَحَداً» وَ هِيَ اَلْجَبْهَةُ وَ اَلْكَفَّانِ وَ اَلرُّكْبَتَانِ وَ اَلْإِبْهَامَانِ وَ وَضْعُ اَلْأَنْفِ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ سُنَّةٌ» ثُمَّ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ اَلسُّجُودِ فَلَمَّا اِسْتَوَى جَالِساً قَالَ« اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ» ثُمَّ قَعَدَ عَلَى فَخِذِهِ اَلْأَيْسَرِ قَدْ وَضَعَ قَدَمَهُ اَلْأَيْمَنَ عَلَى بَطْنِ قَدَمِهِ اَلْأَيْسَرِ وَ قَالَ« أَسْتَغْفِرُ اَللَّهَ رَبِّي وَ أَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ» ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ وَ سَجَدَ سَجْدَةَ اَلثَّانِيَةِ وَ قَالَ كَمَا قَالَ فِي اَلْأُولَى وَ لَمْ يَضَعْ شَيْئاً مِنْ بَدَنِهِ عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ فِي رُكُوعٍ وَلاَ سُجُودٍ وَ كَانَ مُجَّنِّحاً وَ لَمْ يَضَعْ ذِرَاعَيْهِ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ فَصَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ عَلَى هَذَا وَ يَدَاهُ مَضْمُومَةُ اَلْأَصَابِعِ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ فِي اَلتَّشَهُّدِ فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنَ اَلتَّشَهُّدِ سَلَّمَ فَقَالَ« يَا حَمَّادُ هَكَذَا صَلِّ»

items.e: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abd al-Hamid ibn ‘Awwad, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said: I saw Him (a.s), when He (a.s) raised his head from the second prostration of the first rak‘ah, He (a.s) would sit until He (a.s) was at ease, then He (a.s) would stand.
items.o: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ بْنِ عَوَّاضٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُهُ إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ اَلسَّجْدَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ مِنَ اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى جَلَسَ حَتَّى يَطْمَئِنَّ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ

items.e: Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir, who said: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you raise your head from the second prostration in the first rak‘ah, when you intend to stand, then sit upright first, then stand.”
items.o: سَمَاعَةُ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا رَفَعْتَ رَأْسَكَ مِنَ اَلسَّجْدَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى حِينَ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَقُومَ فَاسْتَوِ جَالِساً ثُمَّ قُمْ»

items.e: As for what was narrated by Ali ibn al-Hakam from Rahim, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, I see you, when you pray and raise your head from prostration in the first and third rak‘ah, you sit upright before standing. So should we do as you do?” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not look at what I do, do what you have been commanded to do.”
items.o: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ رَحِيمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أَرَاكَ إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ فَرَفَعْتَ رَأْسَكَ مِنَ اَلسُّجُودِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى وَاَلثَّالِثَةِ تَسْتَوِي جَالِساً ثُمَّ تَقُومُ فَنَصْنَعُ كَمَا تَصْنَعُ قَالَ« لاَ تَنْظُرُوا إِلَى مَا أَصْنَعُ أَنَا اِصْنَعُوا مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ»

items.e: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said: I saw Abu Ja‘far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, when they raised their heads from the second prostration, they stood up without sitting.
items.o: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا رَفَعَا رُءُوسَهُمَا مِنَ اَلسَّجْدَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ نَهَضَا وَ لَمْ يَجْلِسَا

items.e: Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, Ibn Muslim, and al-Halabi said: Imam (a.s) said: “Do not sit in prayer between the two prostrations like the sitting of a dog.”
items.o: مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ عَمَّارٍ وَ اِبْنُ مُسْلِمٍ وَ اَلْحَلَبِيُّ قَالُوا قَالَ:« لاَ تُقْعِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ بَيْنَ اَلسَّجْدَتَيْنِ كَإِقْعَاءِ اَلْكَلْبِ»

items.e: Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said: (Abu Abdillah (a.s) said) “When you sit in prayer, do not sit on your right side, rather, sit on your left side. And when you prostrate, spread your palms on the ground. And when you bow, place your knees into your palms.”
items.o: عَلِيٌّ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا جَلَسْتَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَلاَ تَجْلِسْ عَلَى يَمِينِكَ وَ اِجْلِسْ عَلَى يَسَارِكَ فَإِذَا سَجَدْتَ فَابْسُطْ كَفَّيْكَ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ فَإِذَا رَكَعْتَ فَأَلْقِمْ رُكْبَتَيْكَ كَفَّيْكَ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, and Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you stand in prayer, do not place one foot directly against the other; rather, leave a gap between them, the minimum being the width of a finger, and the maximum up to a span. Let your shoulders hang down, release your arms, and do not interlock your fingers. Let your hands be upon your thighs, opposite your knees, and let your gaze be toward the place of your prostration. When you bow, align your position in bowing between your feet, making the distance between them about a span. Firmly place your palms upon your knees. Place your right hand on your right knee before the left, and let the tips of your fingers reach the center of the kneecap. Spread your fingers when placing them on your knees, and if the tips of your fingers reach in your bowing, reaching your kneecaps, that suffices you. But what is more beloved to me is that you firmly place your palms on your knees, so that your fingers are upon the center of the kneecap, and you spread them apart. Keep your back straight, stretch your neck, and let your gaze be directed to the space between your feet. When you intend to go into prostration, raise your hands with the takbir and go down into prostration, beginning with your hands, place them on the ground before your knees. Place them together. Do not spread your forearms on the ground like a beast spreads its forearms, and do not place your forearms on your knees or thighs. Rather, raise your elbows outward. Do not press your palms to your knees, nor bring them close to your face, let them be level with your shoulders. Do not place them in front of your knees, but turn them slightly away from that. Spread them flat on the ground and draw them toward yourself in a drawing motion. If there is a cloth beneath them, it does not harm you; but if you place them directly on the earth, that is better. Do not spread your fingers during prostration; rather, keep them joined together.” Imam (a.s) said: “When you sit in tashahhud, press your knees to the ground and spread them slightly. Let the top of your left foot be on the ground, and the top of your right foot on the sole of your left foot. Your buttocks should be on the ground, and the tip of your right big toe should be on the ground. Beware of sitting on your two feet, for that causes discomfort, and you will not truly be sitting on the ground, it would be as if you are sitting part of your body upon another part, and you will not be able to remain patient in the tashahhud and in supplication.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ جَمِيعاً عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا قُمْتَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَلاَ تُلْصِقْ قَدَمَكَ بِالْأُخْرَى وَ دَعْ بَيْنَهُمَا فَصْلاً إِصْبَعاً أَقَلُّ ذَلِكَ إِلَى شِبْرٍ أَكْثَرُهُ وَاُسْدُلْ مَنْكِبَيْكَ وَأَرْسِلْ يَدَيْكَ وَلاَ تُشَبِّكْ أَصَابِعَكَ وَلْتَكُونَا عَلَى فَخِذَيْكَ قُبَالَةَ رُكْبَتِكَ وَلْيَكُنْ نَظَرُكَ إِلَى مَوْضِعِ سُجُودِكَ فَإِذَا رَكَعْتَ فَصُفَّ فِي رُكُوعِكَ بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْكَ تَجْعَلُ بَيْنَهُمَا قَدْرَ شِبْرٍ وَ تُمَكِّنُ رَاحَتَيْكَ مِنْ رُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ تَضَعُ يَدَكَ اَلْيُمْنَى عَلَى رُكْبَتِكَ اَلْيُمْنَى قَبْلَ اَلْيُسْرَى وَ بَلِّغْ بِأَطْرَافِ أَصَابِعِكَ عَيْنَ اَلرُّكْبَةِ وَ فَرِّجْ أَصَابِعَكَ إِذَا وَضَعْتَهَا عَلَى رُكْبَتَيْكَ فَإِنْ وَصَلَتْ أَطْرَافُ أَصَابِعِكَ فِي رُكُوعِكَ إِلَى رُكْبَتَيْكَ أَجْزَأَكَ ذَلِكَ وَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ أَنْ تُمَكِّنَ كَفَّيْكَ مِنْ رُكْبَتَيْكَ فَتَجْعَلَ أَصَابِعَكَ فِي عَيْنِ اَلرُّكْبَةِ وَ تُفَرِّجَ بَيْنَهُمَا وَ أَقِمْ صُلْبَكَ وَ مُدَّ عُنُقَكَ وَ لْيَكُنْ نَظَرُكَ إِلَى مَا بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْكَ فَإِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ فَارْفَعْ يَدَيْكَ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ وَخِرَّ سَاجِداً وَاِبْدَأْ بِيَدَيْكَ فَضَعْهُمَا عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ قَبْلَ رُكْبَتَيْكَ تَضَعُهُمَا مَعاً وَ لاَ تَفْتَرِشْ ذِرَاعَيْكَ اِفْتِرَاشَ اَلسَّبُعِ ذِرَاعَيْهِ وَ لاَ تَضَعَنَّ ذِرَاعَيْكَ عَلَى رُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ فَخِذَيْكَ وَ لَكِنْ تَجَنَّحْ بِمِرْفَقَيْكَ وَ لاَ تُلْزِقْ كَفَّيْكَ بِرُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ لاَ تُدْنِهِمَا مِنْ وَجْهِكَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ حِيَالَ مَنْكِبَيْكَ وَ لاَ تَجْعَلْهُمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ لَكِنْ تُحَرِّفُهُمَا عَنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْئاً وَ اُبْسُطْهُمَا عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ بَسْطاً وَ اِقْبِضْهُمَا إِلَيْكَ قَبْضاً وَ إِنْ كَانَ تَحْتَهُمَا ثَوْبٌ فَلاَ يَضُرُّكَ وَ إِنْ أَفْضَيْتَ بِهِمَا إِلَى اَلْأَرْضِ فَهُوَ أَفْضَلُ وَ لاَ تُفَرِّجَنَّ بَيْنَ أَصَابِعِكَ فِي سُجُودِكَ وَ لَكِنِ اُضْمُمْهُنَّ جَمِيعاً قَالَ فَإِذَا قَعَدْتَ فِي تَشَهُّدِكَ فَأَلْصِقْ رُكْبَتَيْكَ بِالْأَرْضِ وَفَرِّجْ بَيْنَهُمَا شَيْئاً وَلْيَكُنْ ظَاهِرُ قَدَمِكَ اَلْيُسْرَى عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ وَظَاهِرُ قَدَمِكَ اَلْيُمْنَى عَلَى بَاطِنِ قَدَمِكَ اَلْيُسْرَى وَأَلْيَتَاكَ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ وَطَرَفُ إِبْهَامِكَ اَلْيُمْنَى عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ وَ إِيَّاكَ وَ اَلْقُعُودَ عَلَى قَدَمَيْكَ فَتَتَأَذَّى بِذَلِكَ وَ لاَ تَكُونُ قَاعِداً عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ فَتَكُونَ إِنَّمَا قَعَدَ بَعْضُكَ عَلَى بَعْضٍ فَلاَ تَصْبِرَ لِلتَّشَهُّدِ وَ اَلدُّعَاءِ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hariz, from a man, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: I said to Him (a.s) regarding the verse: ‘So pray to your Lord and sacrifice”’ (Surah Kawthar 108:2). He (a.s) said: “The ‘nahr’ (sacrifice) is uprightness in standing, that one straightens his back and his neck.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Do not place your hands on your hips (takfir), for that is what the Magians do. Do not cover your mouth (talath-thum), do not squat (ihtifaz), do not sit on your feet (iq‘aʾ), and do not spread your forearms on the ground.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ« فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَ اِنْحَرْ» قَالَ« اَلنَّحْرُ اَلاِعْتِدَالُ فِي اَلْقِيَامِ أَنْ يُقِيمَ صُلْبَهُ وَ نَحْرَهُ» وَ قَالَ« لاَ تُكَفِّرْ إِنَّمَا يَصْنَعُ ذَلِكَ اَلْمَجُوسُ وَ لاَ تَلَثَّمْ وَ لاَ تَحْتَفِزْ وَ لاَ تُقْعِ عَلَى قَدَمَيْكَ وَ لاَ تَفْتَرِشْ ذِرَاعَيْكَ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan, from Fadalah, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said: I asked (Imam (a.s)): “A man places his hand in prayer, (and he demonstrated) the right over the left?. Imam (a.s) said: "That is takfeer (a gesture used by others), so do not do it."
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَضَعُ يَدَهُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ حَكَى اَلْيُمْنَى عَلَى اَلْيُسْرَى فَقَالَ« ذَلِكَ اَلتَّكْفِيرُ فَلاَ تَفْعَلْ»

items.e: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ja‘far ibn Ali, who said: I saw Aba al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, and He (a.s) had performed a prostration after the prayer, and He (a.s) spread his forearms on the ground and pressed his chest to the ground, while still in his clothes.
items.o: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ قَدْ سَجَدَ بَعْدَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَبَسَطَ ذِرَاعَيْهِ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ وَ أَلْصَقَ جُؤْجُؤَهُ بِالْأَرْضِ فِي ثِيَابِهِ

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Khaqan, who said: I saw Aba al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s), peace be upon him, perform the prostration of gratitude (‘Sajdat al-Shukr’), and He (a.s) spread out his forearms and pressed his chest and stomach to the ground. So I asked Him (a.s) about that, and Imam (a.s) said: “This is how it should be.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ خَاقَانَ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلثَّالِثَ عَ سَجَدَ سَجْدَةَ اَلشُّكْرِ فَافْتَرَشَ ذِرَاعَيْهِ وَ أَلْصَقَ صَدْرَهُ وَ بَطْنَهُ فَسَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ« كَذَا يَجِبُ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: I asked Him (a.s) about the limit of prostration. Imam (a.s) said: “Whatever part is placed from the area between the hairline and the position of the eyebrows, it suffices you.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بَحْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ حَدِّ اَلسُّجُودِ قَالَ« مَا بَيْنَ قُصَاصِ اَلشَّعْرِ إِلَى مَوْضِعِ اَلْحَاجِبِ مَا وَضَعْتَ مِنْهُ أَجْزَأَكَ»

items.e: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said: I asked (Imam (a.s)) about a man prostrates while wearing a cap or a turban. Imam (a.s) said: “If his forehead touches the ground in the area between his eyebrows and the hairline, then it suffices for him.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَسْجُدُ وَ عَلَيْهِ قَلَنْسُوَةٌ أَوْ عِمَامَةٌ فَقَالَ« إِذَا مَسَّ جَبْهَتُهُ اَلْأَرْضَ فِيمَا بَيْنَ حَاجِبَيْهِ وَ قُصَاصِ شَعْرِهِ فَقَدْ أَجْزَأَ عَنْهُ

items.e: Al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the place of the forehead of the one prostrating, can it be higher than the place where he stands? Imam (a.s) said: “No, but it should be level.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ مَوْضِعِ جَبْهَةِ اَلسَّاجِدِ أَ يَكُونُ أَرْفَعَ مِنْ مَقَامِهِ فَقَالَ« لاَ وَ لَكِنْ لِيَكُنْ مُسْتَوِياً»

items.e: And from him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from ‘Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who raises the place of his forehead in the mosque (during prostration). Imam (a.s) said: “I like to place my face where my feet stand,” and He (a.s) disliked (raising it).
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ حُمَيْدٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَرْفَعُ مَوْضِعَ جَبْهَتِهِ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ فَقَالَ« إِنِّي أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَضَعَ وَجْهِي فِي مَوْضِعِ قَدَمِي وَ كَرِهَهُ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, from one of his companions, from Musadif, who said: A boil had appeared on me (forehead), so I was prostrating on one side. Abu Abdillah (a.s) saw its mark and said: “What is this?” I said: “I cannot prostrate because of the boil, so I prostrate while turned to the side.” Imam (a.s) said to me: “Do not do that. Dig a small pit and place the boil into the pit so that you may place your forehead on the ground.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنْ مُصَادِفٍ قَالَ: خَرَجَ بِي دُمَّلٌ فَكُنْتُ أَسْجُدُ عَلَى جَانِبٍ فَرَأَى أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَثَرَهُ فَقَالَ« مَا هَذَا» فَقُلْتُ لاَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَسْجُدَ مِنْ أَجْلِ اَلدُّمَّلِ فَإِنَّمَا أَسْجُدُ مُنْحَرِفاً فَقَالَ لِي« لاَ تَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ اِحْفِرْ حَفِيرَةً وَ اِجْعَلِ اَلدُّمَّلَ فِي اَلْحَفِيرَةِ حَتَّى تَضَعَ جَبْهَتَكَ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, by his chain of narration, who said: Abu Abdillah (a.s) was asked about someone who has an ailment on his forehead and is unable to prostrate upon it. Imam (a.s) said: “He should place his chin on the ground, for Allah (swt) the Exalted says: ‘They fall down upon their chins in prostration’.” (Surah Isra 17:107)
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ بِإِسْنَادِهِ قَالَ: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَمَّنْ بِجَبْهَتِهِ عِلَّةٌ لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى اَلسُّجُودِ عَلَيْهَا قَالَ« يَضَعُ ذَقَنَهُ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ إِنَّ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى يَقُولُ« يَخِرُّونَ لِلْأَذْقٰانِ سُجَّداً»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man who prostrates while wearing a turban, such that his forehead does not touch the ground. Imam (a.s) said: “That does not suffice him until his forehead reaches the ground.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَسْجُدُ وَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْعِمَامَةُ لاَ تُصِيبُ جَبْهَتُهُ اَلْأَرْضَ قَالَ« لاَ يُجْزِيهِ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى تَصِلَ جَبْهَتُهُ إِلَى اَلْأَرْضِ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you rise from prostration, say: ‘O Allah (swt), my Lord (azj), by Your (azj) power and strength I rise and I sit.’ And if you wish, you may also say: ‘…and I bow and I prostrate.’”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا قُمْتَ مِنَ اَلسُّجُودِ قُلْتَ اَللَّهُمَّ رَبِّي بِحَوْلِكَ وَ قُوَّتِكَ أَقُومُ وَ أَقْعُدُ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ قُلْتَ وَ أَرْكَعُ وَ أَسْجُدُ»

items.e: And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When a man rises from prostration, he says: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power of Allah (swt) I rise and I sit).’”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا قَامَ اَلرَّجُلُ مِنَ اَلسُّجُودِ قَالَ بِحَوْلِ اَللَّهِ أَقُومُ وَ أَقْعُدُ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sa‘d ibn Abi Khala: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It suffices you in qunut to say: ‘O Allah (swt), forgive us, have mercy on us, grant us well-being, and pardon us in this world and the Hereafter. Indeed, You (azj) have power over all things.’”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ أَبِي خَلَفٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُجْزِيكَ فِي اَلْقُنُوتِ اَللَّهُمَّ اِغْفِرْ لَنَا وَ اِرْحَمْنَا وَ عَافِنَا وَ اُعْفُ عَنَّا فِي اَلدُّنْيَا وَ اَلْآخِرَةِ« إِنَّكَ عَلىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ»

items.e: What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The takbir in the obligatory prayer, in the five daily prayers, is ninety-five takbirs, among them are five takbirs of qunut.”
items.o: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ:« اَلتَّكْبِيرُ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْفَرْضِ فِي اَلْخَمْسِ اَلصَّلَوَاتِ خَمْسٌ وَ تِسْعُونَ تَكْبِيرَةً مِنْهَا تَكْبِيرَةُ اَلْقُنُوتِ خَمْسٌ»

items.e: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah: Imam (a.s) explained the (takbirs) as follows; In Dhuhr, twenty-one takbirs; in ‘Asr, twenty-one takbirs; in Maghrib, sixteen takbirs; in the last Isha, twenty-one takbirs; and in Fajr, eleven takbirs; and five takbirs of qunut in the five prayers.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ:« وَ فَسَّرَهُنَّ فِي اَلظُّهْرِ إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرُونَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ فِي اَلْعَصْرِ إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرُونَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ فِي اَلْمَغْرِبِ سِتَّ عَشْرَةَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ فِي اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرُونَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ فِي اَلْفَجْرِ إِحْدَى عَشْرَةَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ خَمْسُ تَكْبِيرَاتِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فِي خَمْسِ صَلَوَاتٍُ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn ‘Umar, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from al-Sabbah al-Muzani, who said Commander of the Faithful, (Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s)), peace be upon him, said: “Ninety-five takbirs are (prescribed) in the day and night for the prayers, among them is the takbir of qunut.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عُمَرَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ اَلصَّبَّاحِ اَلْمُزَنِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« خَمْسٌ وَ تِسْعُونَ تَكْبِيرَةً فِي اَلْيَوْمِ وَ اَللَّيْلَةِ لِلصَّلَوَاتِ مِنْهَا تَكْبِيرَةُ اَلْقُنُوتِ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you sit after the first two rak‘ahs and recite the tashahhud, then stand, say: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power and strength of Allah (swt) I rise and I sit.)”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا جَلَسْتَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأُولَيَيْنِ فَتَشَهَّدْتَ ثُمَّ قُمْتَ فَقُلْ بِحَوْلِ اَللَّهِ وَ قُوَّتِهِ أَقُومُ وَ أَقْعُدُ»

items.e: And from him, from Fadalah, from Rifa‘ah ibn Musa, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “When (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, would rise from the first two rak‘ahs, He (a.s) would say: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power and strength of Allah (swt) I rise and I sit.)”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ بْنِ مُوسَى قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« كَانَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا نَهَضَ مِنَ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأُولَيَيْنِ قَالَ« بِحَوْلِكَ وَ قُوَّتِكَ أَقُومُ وَ أَقْعُدُ»»

items.e: And from him, from Fadalah, from Sayf, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you rise from the two rak‘ahs, lean on your palms and say: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power and strength of Allah (swt) I rise and I sit.) for indeed (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, used to do that.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ سَيْفٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ اَلْحَضْرَمِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا قُمْتَ مِنَ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ فَاعْتَمِدْ عَلَى كَفَّيْكَ وَ قُلْ بِحَوْلِ اَللَّهِ أَقُومُ وَ أَقْعُدُ فَإِنَّ عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَانَ يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (a.s) for several days, and He (a.s) would perform ‘qunut’ in every prayer, whether it was one in which the recitation was audible or not.
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ اَلْجَمَّالِ قَالَ: صَلَّيْتُ خَلْفَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَيَّاماً فَكَانَ يَقْنُتُ فِي كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا أَوْلاَ يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا

items.e: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Qunut is in every prayer, in the second rak‘ah, before bowing.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْقُنُوتُ فِي كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ»

items.e: And from him, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘qunut’ in all five prayers. Imam (a.s) said: “Perform ‘qunut’ in all of them.” He (Muhammad ibn Muslim) said: “Then I later asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about that, and Imam (a.s) said: “As for the prayers in which you recite aloud, do not have any doubt about it.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ وَ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فِي اَلصَّلَوَاتِ اَلْخَمْسِ جَمِيعاً فَقَالَ« اُقْنُتْ فِيهِنَّ جَمِيعاً» قَالَ فَسَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بَعْدُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ« أَمَّا مَا جَهَرْتَ فِيهِ فَلاَ تَشُكَّ»

items.e: And from him, from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Qunut in Maghrib is in the second rak‘ah, and in Isha and Ghadah (Fajr) it is the same. And in Witr it is in the third rak‘ah.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْقُنُوتُ فِي اَلْمَغْرِبِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ وَ فِي اَلْعِشَاءِ وَ اَلْغَدَاةِ مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ وَ فِي اَلْوَتْرِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّالِثَةِ»

items.e: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Zur‘ah, from Sama‘ah, who said: I asked Him (a.s) about ‘qunut’, about which prayer is it in? Imam (a.s) said: “Every prayer in which the recitation is done aloud has ‘qunut’ in it, and ‘qunut’ is before bowing and after the recitation.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فِي أَيِّ صَلاَةٍ هُوَ فَقَالَ« كُلُّ شَيْءٍ يُجْهَرُ فِيهِ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ فِيهِ قُنُوتٌ وَ اَلْقُنُوتُ قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ بَعْدَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ»

items.e: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said: One of our companions asked Him (a.s), and I (Abu Basir) was present, about ‘qunut’ in the Friday prayer. Imam (a.s) said to him: “In the second rak‘ah.” So the man said to Him (a.s): “One of our companions narrated to us that you told him it is in the first rak‘ah.” Imam (a.s) said: “In the last.” Then, when He (a.s) saw that the man was confused, Imam (a.s) said: “O Aba Muhammad, (it is) in both the first and the last.” Then Abu Basir asked after that: “Is it before the bowing or after it?” So Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Every ‘qunut’ is before bowing, except in Friday prayer: in the first rak‘ah it is before bowing, and in the last it is after bowing.”
items.o: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلَهُ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا وَ أَنَا عِنْدَهُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فِي اَلْجُمُعَةِ فَقَالَ لَهُ« فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ» فَقَالَ لَهُ قَدْ حَدَّثَنَا بِهِ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا أَنَّكَ قُلْتَ لَهُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى فَقَالَ« فِي اَلْأَخِيرَةِ» فَلَمَّا رَأَى غَفْلَةً مِنْهُ فَقَالَ« يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ فِي اَلْأُولَى وَ اَلْأَخِيرَةِ» فَقَالَ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَ قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ أَوْ بَعْدَهُ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« كُلُّ قُنُوتٍ قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ إِلاَّ اَلْجُمُعَةَ فَإِنَّ اَلرَّكْعَةَ اَلْأُولَى فِيهَا قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلْأَخِيرَةَ بَعْدَ اَلرُّكُوعِ»

items.e: And from him, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Wahb: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “Qunut is in Friday prayer, Isha, ‘Atamah (night prayer), Witr, and Ghadah (Fajr). Whoever abandons qunut out of aversion to it, then he has no prayer.”
items.o: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ وَهْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْقُنُوتُ فِي اَلْجُمُعَةِ وَاَلْعِشَاءِ وَاَلْعَتَمَةِ وَاَلْوَتْرِ وَ اَلْغَدَاةِ فَمَنْ تَرَكَ اَلْقُنُوتَ رَغْبَةً عَنْهُ فَلاَ صَلاَةَ لَهُ»

items.e: And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Qunut is in every two rak‘ahs, in supererogatory (nafl) and obligatory prayers.” Al-Hasan said: “And Abdullah ibn Bukayr informed me from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Qunut is in all prayers.” Muhammad ibn Muslim said: “So I mentioned that to Abu Abdillah (a.s), and Imam (a.s) said: “As for that in which there is no doubt, it is what is recited aloud.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «اَلْقُنُوتُ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فِي اَلتَّطَوُّعِ وَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ» قَالَ اَلْحَسَنُ وَ أَخْبَرَنِي عَبْدُ اَللَّهِ بْنُ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: قَالَ« اَلْقُنُوتُ فِي كُلِّ اَلصَّلَوَاتِ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ فَذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ« أَمَّا مَا لاَ يُشَكُّ فِيهِ فَمَا جُهِرَ فِيهِ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ»

items.e: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Amr, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about ‘qunut’, is it before bowing or after? Imam (a.s) said: “Neither before it nor after it.”
items.o: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ صَالِحٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ أَوْ بَعْدَهُ قَالَ« لاَ قَبْلَهُ وَ لاَ بَعْدَهُ»

items.e: And from him, from al-Barqi, from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: I asked Him (a.s) about ‘qunut’, is ‘qunut’ performed in all the prayers, or only in those in which the recitation is audible? Imam (a.s) said: “Qunut is only in Ghadah (Fajr), Jumu‘ah (Friday prayer), Witr, and Maghrib.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ هَلْ يُقْنَتُ فِي اَلصَّلَوَاتِ كُلِّهَا أَمْ فِيمَا يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ قَالَ« لَيْسَ اَلْقُنُوتُ إِلاَّ فِي اَلْغَدَاةِ وَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ وَ اَلْوَتْرِ وَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ».

items.e: Sa‘d ibn Abdullah narrated from Abu Ja‘far, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): In which prayers should I perform ‘qunut’? Imam (a.s) said: “Do not perform ‘qunut’ except in Fajr.”
items.o: وَ رَوَى سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فِي أَيِّ اَلصَّلَوَاتِ أَقْنُتُ فَقَالَ« لاَ تَقْنُتْ إِلاَّ فِي اَلْفَجْرِ»

items.e: Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding ‘qunut’: “If you wish, then perform qunut; and if you wish, do not perform it.” Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘And when there is taqiyyah (precautionary dissimulation), then do not perform qunut, and I adhere to this.’
items.o: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي اَلْقُنُوتِ:« إِنْ شِئْتَ فَاقْنُتْ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ لاَ تَقْنُتْ» قَالَ أَبُو اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« وَ إِذَا كَانَتِ اَلتَّقِيَّةُ فَلاَ تَقْنُتْ وَ أَنَا أَتَقَلَّدُ هَذَا»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about ‘qunut’. Imam (a.s) said: “In that which you recite aloud.” So I said: “I asked your father (a.s) about that, and Imam (a.s) said: ‘In all five prayers.’” Imam (a.s) said: “May Allah (swt) have mercy on my father (a.s). The companions of my father (a.s) came to him and asked him, so He (a.s) informed them of the truth. Then they came to me full of doubts, so I gave them a ruling based on ‘taqiyyah’ (precautionary dissimulation).”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فَقَالَ« فِيمَا تَجْهَرُ فِيهِ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ» قَالَ فَقُلْتُ إِنِّي سَأَلْتُ أَبَاكَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ« فِي اَلْخَمْسِ كُلِّهَا» فَقَالَ« رَحِمَ اَللَّهُ أَبِي إِنَّ أَصْحَابَ أَبِي أَتَوْهُ فَسَأَلُوهُ فَأَخْبَرَهُمْ بِالْحَقِّ ثُمَّ أَتَوْنِي شُكَّاكاً فَأَفْتَيْتُهُمْ بِالتَّقِيَّةِ»

items.e: Sa‘d, from Abu Ja‘far, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, who said: Abu al-Qasim Mu‘awiyah narrated to me from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Sammak, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said: Imam (a.s) said to me regarding the ‘qunut’ of ‘witr’: ‘O Allah (swt), forgive us, have mercy on us, grant us well-being, and pardon us in this world and the Hereafter.‘ And Imam (a.s) said: ‘Three tasbihat suffice for qunut.”’
items.o: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو اَلْقَاسِمِ مُعَاوِيَةُ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ أَبِي سَمَّاكٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ لِي: فِي قُنُوتِ اَلْوَتْرِ« اَللَّهُمَّ اِغْفِرْ لَنَا وَ اِرْحَمْنَا وَ عَافِنَا وَ اُعْفُ عَنَّا فِي اَلدُّنْيَا وَ اَلْآخِرَةِ» وَ قَالَ« يُجْزِي مِنَ اَلْقُنُوتِ ثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ»

items.e: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Aban ibn ‘Uthman, from Isma‘il al-Ju‘fi and Ma‘mar ibn Yahya: Abu Ja‘far (a.s) said: “Qunut is before bowing, and if you wish, then after it.”
items.o: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْجَوْهَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ اَلْجُعْفِيِّ وَمَعْمَرِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْقُنُوتُ قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ فَبَعْدَهُ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan: Abdullah ibn Bukayr narrated to us from Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Amr al-Ahwal: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The ‘tashahhud’ in the first two rak‘ahs is: ‘Alhamdu lillah ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa taqabbal shafaatahu fi ummatih wa irfa darajatah’ (I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is His servant and messenger. O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and accept His (saws) intercession on behalf of His (saws) nation, and raise His (saws) rank.’”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اَللَّهِ بْنُ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو اَلْأَحْوَلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلتَّشَهُّدُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأُولَيَيْنِ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ تَقَبَّلْ شَفَاعَتَهُ فِي أُمَّتِهِ وَ اِرْفَعْ دَرَجَتَهُ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibrahim al-Khazzaz, from Abd al-Hamid ibn ‘Awwad: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If you are leading a group in prayer, one ‘taslim’ to your right suffices. If you are praying behind an imam, then (you do) two ‘taslims’. And if you are alone, then one ‘taslim’ facing the qiblah suffices.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ بْنِ عَوَّاضٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنْ كُنْتَ تَؤُمُّ قَوْماً أَجْزَأَكَ تَسْلِيمَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ عَنْ يَمِينِكَ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ مَعَ إِمَامٍ فَتَسْلِيمَتَيْنِ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ فَوَاحِدَةً مُسْتَقْبِلَ اَلْقِبْلَةِ»

items.e: And from him, from Safwan, from Mansur, who said: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The imam says one ‘taslim’, and those behind him say two ‘taslims’. But if there is no one on his left, then he says one ‘taslim’.”
items.o: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« اَلْإِمَامُ يُسَلِّمُ وَاحِدَةً وَمَنْ وَرَاءَهُ يُسَلِّمُ اِثْنَتَيْنِ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَنْ شِمَالِهِ أَحَدٌ سَلَّمَ وَاحِدَةً»

items.e: And from him, from Fadalah, from Husayn, from Ibn Muskan, from ‘Anbasah ibn Mus‘ab, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about a man standing in the row behind the imam and there is no one on his left, how should he perform the ‘taslim’? Imam (a.s) said: “One ‘taslim’ to his right.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ عَنْبَسَةَ بْنِ مُصْعَبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَقُومُ فِي اَلصَّفِّ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى يَسَارِهِ أَحَدٌ كَيْفَ يُسَلِّمُ قَالَ« تَسْلِيمَةً عَنْ يَمِينِهِ»

items.e: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Ma‘mar ibn Yahya, and Isma‘il: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “He performs one ‘taslim’, whether he is an imam or not.”
items.o: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَ مَعْمَرِ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُسَلِّمُ تَسْلِيمَةً وَاحِدَةً إِمَاماً كَانَ أَوْ غَيْرَهُ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If you are an imam, then the ‘taslim’ is that you send salam upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and say: ‘Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah (swt).’ Once you say that, the prayer has ended. Then you inform the people by saying, while facing the qiblah, ‘Peace be upon you.’ And likewise, if you are praying alone, you say: ‘Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah (swt) ‘ just as you would say if you were the imam. But if you are in a congregation, then say what you have said, and send salam upon those on your right and your left. If there is no one on your left, then send salam upon those on your right, and do not omit sending ‘taslim’ to your right even if there is no one on your left.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا كُنْتَ إِمَاماً فَإِنَّمَا اَلتَّسْلِيمُ أَنْ تُسَلِّمَ عَلَى اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَتَقُولَ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اَللَّهِ اَلصَّالِحِينَ فَإِذَا قُلْتَ ذَلِكَ فَقَدِ اِنْقَطَعَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ ثُمَّ تُؤْذِنُ اَلْقَوْمَ فَتَقُولُ وَ أَنْتَ مُسْتَقْبِلُ اَلْقِبْلَةَ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَ كَذَلِكَ إِذَا كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ تَقُولُ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْنَا وَ عَلَى عِبَادِ اَللَّهِ اَلصَّالِحِينَ مِثْلَ مَا سَلَّمْتَ وَ أَنْتَ إِمَامٌ فَإِذَا كُنْتَ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ فَقُلْ مِثْلَ مَا قُلْتَ وَ سَلِّمْ عَلَى مَنْ عَلَى يَمِينِكَ وَ شِمَالِكَ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَى شِمَالِكَ أَحَدٌ فَسَلِّمْ عَلَى اَلَّذِينَ عَلَى يَمِينِكَ وَ لاَ تَدَعِ اَلتَّسْلِيمَ عَلَى يَمِينِكَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَى شِمَالِكَ أَحَدٌ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah: (It was said) “When a woman stands for prayer, she joins her feet together and does not spread them apart, and she brings her hands close to her chest due to the presence of her breasts. When she bows, she places her hands above her knees, on her thighs, so that she does not bend too much and raise her backside. When she sits, she sits on her buttocks as a man does. When she moves into prostration, she begins by sitting and placing her knees down before her hands. Then she prostrates closely to the ground. When she is in her sitting posture, she brings her thighs together and lifts her knees off the ground. When she rises, she rises smoothly, without first lifting her backside.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ:« إِذَا قَامَتِ اَلْمَرْأَةُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ جَمَعَتْ بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْهَا وَ لاَ تُفَرِّجُ بَيْنَهُمَا وَ تَضُمُّ يَدَيْهَا إِلَى صَدْرِهَا لِمَكَانِ ثَدْيَيْهَا فَإِذَا رَكَعَتْ وَضَعَتْ يَدَيْهَا فَوْقَ رُكْبَتَيْهَا عَلَى فَخِذَيْهَا لِئَلاَّ تَطَأْطَأَ كَثِيراً فَتَرْتَفِعَ عَجِيزَتُهَا فَإِذَا جَلَسَتْ فَعَلَى أَلْيَتَيْهَا كَمَا يَقْعُدُ اَلرَّجُلُ فَإِذَا سَقَطَتْ لِلسُّجُودِ بَدَأَتْ بِالْقُعُودِ وَ بِالرُّكْبَتَيْنِ قَبْلَ اَلْيَدَيْنِ ثُمَّ تَسْجُدُ لاَطِئَةً بِالْأَرْضِ فَإِذَا كَانَتْ فِي جُلُوسِهَا ضَمَّتْ فَخِذَيْهَا وَ رَفَعَتْ رُكْبَتَيْهَا مِنَ اَلْأَرْضِ فَإِذَا نَهَضَتْ اِنْسَلَّتْ اِنْسِلاَلاً لاَ تَرْفَعُ عَجِيزَتَهَا أَوَّلاً»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When a woman prostrates, she spreads her forearms.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا سَجَدَتِ اَلْمَرْأَةُ بَسَطَتْ ذِرَاعَيْهَا»

items.e: And from him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Him (a.s) about the sitting posture of a woman in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “She brings her thighs together.”
items.o: عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ جُلُوسِ اَلْمَرْأَةِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« تَضُمُّ فَخِذَيْهَا»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions: (It was said): “When a woman prostrates, she gathers herself (draws herself in), and when a man prostrates, he spreads himself out.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا قَالَ: «اَلْمَرْأَةُ إِذَا سَجَدَتْ تَضَمَّمَتْ وَ اَلرَّجُلُ إِذَا سَجَدَ تَفَتَّحَ»

items.e: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Is there anything specific or fixed regarding the recitation in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, except for Jumu‘ah, ‘(Surah) al-Jumu‘ah’ and ‘(Surah) al-Munafiqin’ are to be recited.” I said to Him (a.s): “Then which surahs should be recited in the prayers?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for Dhuhr and the final Isha, they are the same; and ‘Asr and Maghrib are the same. As for Ghadah (Fajr), it is the longest. As for Dhuhr and the final Isha, then (recite): ‘Sabbih isma Rabbika al-A‘la’ (Surah Al-A‘la) and ‘al-Shamsi wa Duhaha’ (Surah Al-Shams), and those like them. And as for ‘Asr and Maghrib, then (recite): ‘Idha ja’a nasrullah’ (Surah An-Nasr) and ‘Alhakum al-Takathur’ (Surah At-Takathur), and those like them. And as for Ghadah (Fajr), then (recite): ‘Amma yatasaa’alun’ (Surah An-Naba’), ‘Hal ataka hadithu’l-ghashiyah’ (Surah Al-Ghashiyah), ‘La uqsimu biyawm al-qiyamah’ (Surah Al-Qiyamah), and ‘Hal ata ‘ala’l-insani hinun mina’l-dahr’ (Surah Al-Insan).”
items.o: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلْقِرَاءَةُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فِيهَا شَيْءٌ مُوَقَّتٌ قَالَ« لاَ إِلاَّ اَلْجُمُعَةَ تُقْرَأُ بِالْجُمُعَةِ وَ اَلْمُنَافِقِينَ» قُلْتُ لَهُ فَأَيُّ اَلسُّوَرِ تُقْرَأُ فِي اَلصَّلَوَاتِ قَالَ« أَمَّا اَلظُّهْرُ وَ اَلْعِشَاءُ اَلْآخِرَةُ تُقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا سَوَاءً وَ اَلْعَصْرُ وَ اَلْمَغْرِبُ سَوَاءً وَ أَمَّا اَلْغَدَاةُ فَأَطْوَلُ وَ أَمَّا اَلظُّهْرُ وَ اَلْعِشَاءُ اَلْآخِرَةُ فَ«سَبِّحِ اِسْمَ رَبِّكَ اَلْأَعْلَى» وَ «اَلشَّمْسِ وَ ضُحٰاهٰا» وَ نَحْوُهُمَا وَ أَمَّا اَلْعَصْرُ وَ اَلْمَغْرِبُ فَ«إِذٰا جٰاءَ نَصْرُ اَللّٰهِ» وَ «أَلْهٰاكُمُ اَلتَّكٰاثُرُ» وَ نَحْوُهُمَا وَ أَمَّا اَلْغَدَاةُ فَ«عَمَّ يَتَسٰاءَلُونَ» وَ «هَلْ أَتٰاكَ حَدِيثُ اَلْغٰاشِيَةِ» وَ« لاٰ أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ اَلْقِيٰامَةِ» وَ« هَلْ أَتىٰ عَلَى اَلْإِنْسٰانِ حِينٌ مِنَ اَلدَّهْرِ»

items.e: And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Aban ibn Isa ibn Abdillah al-Qummi: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, used to pray Ghadah (Fajr) with: ‘Amma yatasaa’alun’ (Surah An-Naba), ‘Hal ataka hadithu’l-ghashiyah’ (Surah Al-Ghashiyah), ‘La uqsimu biyawm al-qiyamah’ (Surah Al-Qiyamah), and similar surahs. And He (a.s) used to pray Dhuhr with: ‘Sabbih isma Rabbika al-A‘la’ (Surah Al-A‘la), ‘al-Shamsi wa Duhaha’ (Surah Al-Shams), ‘Hal ataka hadithu’l-ghashiyah’ (Surah Al-Ghashiyah), and similar surahs. And He (a.s) used to pray Maghrib with: ‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas), ‘Idha ja’a nasrullah wa’l-fath’ (Surah An-Nasr), ‘Idha zulzilati’l-ardu zilzalaha’ (Surah Az-Zalzalah). And He (a.s) used to pray the final Isha similarly to how He (a.s) prayed Dhuhr, and ‘Asr similarly to how He (a.s) prayed Maghrib.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْقُمِّيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يُصَلِّي اَلْغَدَاةَ بِ«عَمَّ يَتَسٰاءَلُونَ» وَ «هَلْ أَتٰاكَ حَدِيثُ اَلْغٰاشِيَةِ» وَ «لاٰ أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ اَلْقِيٰامَةِ» وَ شِبْهِهَا وَ كَانَ يُصَلِّي اَلظُّهْرَ بِ«سَبِّحِ اِسْمَ» وَ «اَلشَّمْسِ وَ ضُحٰاهٰا» وَ «هَلْ أَتٰاكَ حَدِيثُ اَلْغٰاشِيَةِ» وَ شِبْهِهَا وَ كَانَ يُصَلِّي اَلْمَغْرِبَ بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ «إِذٰا جٰاءَ نَصْرُ اَللّٰهِ وَ اَلْفَتْحُ» وَ «إِذٰا زُلْزِلَتِ» وَ كَانَ يُصَلِّي اَلْعِشَاءَ اَلْآخِرَةَ بِنَحْوِ مَا يُصَلِّي فِي اَلظُّهْرِ وَ اَلْعَصْرَ بِنَحْوٍ مِنَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ»

items.e: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: Abu Abdillah (a.s) instructed me to recite ‘al-Mu‘awwidhatayn’ (‘Surat al-Falaq’ and ‘Surat al-Nas’) in the obligatory prayer.
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ قَالَ: أَمَرَنِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ اَلْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ.

items.e: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Sabir, the freed slave of Bassam, who said: Abu Abdillah (a.s) led us in the Maghrib prayer, and He (a.s) recited ‘al-Mu‘awwidhatayn’ (‘Surat al-Falaq’ and ‘Surat al-Nas’).
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سَيْفٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ فَرْقَدٍ عَنْ صَابِرٍ مَوْلَى بَسَّامٍ قَالَ: أَمَّنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَقَرَأَ اَلْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ

items.e: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Isma‘il ibn Abd al-Khaliq, from Abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn Abi Talhah, the maternal uncle of Sahl ibn Abd Rabbih: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “I recited in the Fajr prayer: ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Al-Ikhlas) and ‘Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun’ (Surah Al-Kafirun), and the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, also did that.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْخَالِقِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ خَالِ سَهْلِ بْنِ عَبْدِ رَبِّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «قَرَأْتُ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ «قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ» وَ قَدْ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ»

items.e: And from him, from Abu Sa‘id al-Mukari and Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah and Abu Ishaq Tha‘labah, from Zurarah, who said: I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I pray using : ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Al-Ikhlas)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, prayed in both rak‘ahs with ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’, and He (saws) did not pray before it or after it with anything more complete than it.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ اَلْمُكَارِي وَ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ وَ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ ثَعْلَبَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أُصَلِّي بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ قَدْ صَلَّى رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فِي كِلْتَا اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ لَمْ يُصَلِّ قَبْلَهَا وَ لاَ بَعْدَهَا بِ«قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» أَتَمَّ مِنْهَا»

items.e: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ suffices for fifty prayers.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ اَلْجَمَّالِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:«« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» تُجْزِي فِي خَمْسِينَ صَلاَةً»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said: (Imam (a.s) said) “Do not recite anything from the ‘Azaʾim’ (chapters containing obligatory prostration) in the obligatory prayer, for prostration is an addition in the obligatory prayer.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ تَقْرَأْ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ اَلْعَزَائِمِ فَإِنَّ اَلسُّجُودَ زِيَادَةٌ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Yusuf ibn ‘Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s) (peace be upon him), who said: (imam (a.s) said) “Commander of the Faithful, (Imam Ali Ibn Abi Talib (a.s)), peace be upon him, when He (a.s) prayed, would recite silently in the first two rak‘ahs of his Dhuhr prayer, and He (a.s) would perform ‘tasbih’ (glorification) in the last two rak‘ahs of his Dhuhr prayer, similar to what He (a.s) did in the Isha prayer. And He (a.s) would recite silently in the first two rak‘ahs of his ‘Asr prayer, and He (a.s) would perform ‘tasbih’ in the last two rak‘ahs similar to what He (a.s) did in the Isha prayer. And He (a.s) used to say: ‘The beginning of the prayer of one of you is the bowing.’”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُوسُفَ بْنِ عَقِيلٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا صَلَّى يَقْرَأُ فِي اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ اَلظُّهْرِ سِرّاً وَ يُسَبِّحُ فِي اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ اَلظُّهْرِ عَلَى نَحْوٍ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ اَلْعِشَاءِ وَ كَانَ يَقْرَأُ فِي اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْعَصْرِ سِرّاً وَ يُسَبِّحُ فِي اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ عَلَى نَحْوٍ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْعِشَاءِ وَ كَانَ يَقُولُ أَوَّلُ صَلاَةِ أَحَدِكُمُ اَلرُّكُوعُ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah and Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: “Nothing of recitation or supplication is recorded except what he makes himself hear.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ وَ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ يُكْتَبُ مِنَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ وَ اَلدُّعَاءِ إِلاَّ مَا أَسْمَعَ نَفْسَهُ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri’ab, from al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “May a man recite in his prayer while his garment is over his mouth?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no problem with that, as long as he makes his ears hear the murmur (of his recitation).”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ هَلْ يَقْرَأُ اَلرَّجُلُ فِي صَلاَتِهِ وَ ثَوْبُهُ عَلَى فِيهِ قَالَ« فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ إِذَا أَسْمَعَ أُذُنَيْهِ اَلْهَمْهَمَةَ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-‘Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja‘far (peace be upon them both), who said: I asked Him (a.s) about a man, is it permissible for him to recite in his prayer and move his tongue with the recitation only within his throat without making himself hear it? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm if he does not move his tongue and simply imagines (the recitation) as imagination.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَصْلُحُ لَهُ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ فِي صَلاَتِهِ وَ يُحَرِّكَ لِسَانَهُ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ فِي لَهَوَاتِهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يُسْمِعَ نَفْسَهُ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ لاَ يُحَرِّكَ لِسَانَهُ يَتَوَهَّمُ تَوَهُّماً»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from someone who mentioned it: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It suffices you, when praying with them, to recite like the whispering of the soul (inner speech).”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُجْزِيكَ مِنَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ مَعَهُمْ مِثْلُ حَدِيثِ اَلنَّفْسِ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said: I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “What suffices in terms of recitation in the last two rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: “That you say: ‘Subhan Allah, wal-hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illa Allah, wa-Allahu akbar’, then you say the ‘takbir’ and bow.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَا يُجْزِي مِنَ اَلْقَوْلِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ قَالَ« أَنْ تَقُولَ سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ وَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ وَ تُكَبِّرَ وَ تَرْكَعَ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Halabi, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about the last two rak‘ahs of Dhuhr. Imam (a.s) said: “You glorify (‘tusabbih’), praise Allah (swt) (‘tuhammid’), and seek forgiveness for your sins. And if you wish, recite the Opening of the Book (‘Surat al-Fatihah’), for it is praise and supplication.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلظُّهْرِ قَالَ« تُسَبِّحُ وَ تُحَمِّدُ اَللَّهَ وَ تَسْتَغْفِرُ لِذَنْبِكَ وَإِنْ شِئْتَ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ فَإِنَّهَا تَحْمِيدٌ وَ دُعَاءٌ»

items.e: Sa‘d, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ali ibn Hanzalah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said: I asked Him (a.s) about the last two rak‘ahs, what should I do in them? Imam (a.s) said: “If you wish, recite the Opening of the Book (‘Surat al-Fatihah’), and if you wish, remember Allah (swt), it is the same.” I asked: “Which of the two is better?” Imam (a.s) said: “By Allah (swt), they are the same. If you wish, you may glorify (‘tasbih’), and if you wish, you may recite.”
items.o: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَنْظَلَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ مَا أَصْنَعُ فِيهِمَا فَقَالَ« إِنْ شِئْتَ فَاقْرَأْ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ فَاذْكُرِ اَللَّهَ فَهُوَ سَوَاءٌ» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَأَيُّ ذَلِكَ أَفْضَلُ فَقَالَ« هُمَا وَ اَللَّهِ سَوَاءٌ إِنْ شِئْتَ سَبَّحْتَ وَإِنْ شِئْتَ قَرَأْتَ»

items.e: This was narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn ‘Allan, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “Which is better in the last two rak‘ahs, recitation or ‘tasbih’?” Imam (a.s) said: “Recitation is better.”
items.o: رَوَى ذَلِكَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلاَّنٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَيُّمَا أَفْضَلُ اَلْقِرَاءَةُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ أَوِ اَلتَّسْبِيحُ فَقَالَ« اَلْقِرَاءَةُ أَفْضَلُ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If you are an imam (of prayer), then recite the Opening of the Book (‘Surat al-Fatihah’) in the last two rak‘ahs. And if you are alone, then it is permissible whether you do so or not.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا كُنْتَ إِمَاماً فَاقْرَأْ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ فَيَسَعُكَ فَعَلْتَ أَوْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ»

items.e: As for what was narrated by Sa‘d, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “If you stand for the last two rak‘ahs, do not recite in them. Rather, say: ‘al-hamdu lillah’, ‘subhan Allah’, and ‘Allahu akbar’.”
items.o: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا قُمْتَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ لاَ تَقْرَأْ فِيهِمَا فَقُلِ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ وَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Zur‘ah, from Abu Basir: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you sit in the second rak‘ah, say: ‘Bismi Allah wa billah wa alhamdu lillah wa khayru al-asmai lillah ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh arsalahu bil-haqqi bashiran wa nadhiran bayna yadayi al-sa'ah ashhadu annaka ni'ma al-rabb wa anna Muhammadan ni'ma al-rasul Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa taqabbal shafaatahu fi ummatih wa irfa darajatah’ (In the Name of Allah (swt), and by Allah (swt), and all praise is due to Allah (swt), and the best of names belong to Allah (swt). I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone, without any partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is His servant and His messenger. He (swt) sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner before the Hour. I bear witness that You (swt) are the best Lord (swt), and that Muhammad (saws) is the best messenger. O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and accept his intercession for his nation, and raise his rank.) Then you praise Allah (swt) twice or three times, then rise. And when you sit in the fourth (rak‘ah), you say: ‘Bismi Allah wa billah wa alhamdu lillah wa khayru al-asmai lillah ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh arsalahu bil-haqqi bashiran wa nadhiran bayna yadayi al-sa'ah ashhadu annaka ni'ma al-rabb wa anna Muhammadan ni'ma al-rasul al-tahiyyatu lillah wa al-salawatu al-tahiratu al-tayyibatu al-zakiyatu al-ghadiyatu al-raihat al-sabi ghat al-na'imatu lillah ma taba wa zaka wa tahura wa khalasa wa safa falillah wa ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah. Wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh arsalahu bil-haqqi bashiran wa nadhiran bayna yadayi al-sa'ah ashhadu anna rabbi ni'ma al-rabb wa anna Muhammadan ni'ma al-rasul wa ashhadu anna al-sa'ata atiyatun la rayba fiha wa anna Allah yab'athu man fi al-qubur’” (In the Name of Allah (swt), and by Allah (swt), and all praise is due to Allah (swt), and the best of names belong to Allah (swt). I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone, without any partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is His servant and His messenger. He (swt) sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner before the Hour. I bear witness that You (swt) are the best Lord (swt), and that Muhammad (saws) is the best messenger. All greetings are for Allah (swt), and the pure, good, blessed, ascending and descending, complete and delightful prayers are for Allah (swt) whatever is good, pure, purified, sincere, and clear belongs to Allah (swt) and is for Allah (swt). And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone, without any partner. And I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is His servant and His messenger. He (swt) sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner before the Hour. I bear witness that my Lord (swt) is the best Lord (swt), and that Muhammad (saws) is the best messenger. And I bear witness “that the Hour is surely coming there is no doubt about it and that Allah (swt) will resurrect those who are in the graves.” All praise is due to Allah (swt) who has guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had Allah (swt) not guided us. All praise is due to Allah (swt), the Lord of the worlds." “O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and bless Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and send peace upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and have mercy on Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), just as You (azj) sent blessings and bestowed favor and mercy upon Ibrahim (a.s) and upon the family of Ibrahim (a.s), indeed, You (azj) are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws) and Forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place not in our hearts any resentment toward those who believe, our Lord (azj), indeed You are Kind and Merciful. O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and grant me Paradise by Your (swt) grace and protect me from the Fire. O Allah (swt), send blessings upon Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws) and forgive the believing men and believing women; And those who enter my house as believers, and the believing men and the believing women, and increase not the wrongdoers except in destruction."‘ Then say: ‘Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His blessings.’ ‘Peace be upon the Prophets of Allah (swt) and His messengers.’ ‘Peace be upon Jibra’il (a.s) and Mika’il (a.s) and the close angels.’ ‘Peace be upon Muhammad ibn Abdillah (saws), the Seal of the Prophets, there is no prophet after him.’ ‘And peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah (swt).’ Then you give the salam (salutation to conclude the prayer).
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا جَلَسْتَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ فَقُلْ بِسْمِ اَللَّهِ وَ بِاللَّهِ وَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ خَيْرُ اَلْأَسْمَاءِ لِلَّهِ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ أَرْسَلَهُ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيراً وَ نَذِيراً بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اَلسَّاعَةِ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّكَ نِعْمَ اَلرَّبُّ وَ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً نِعْمَ اَلرَّسُولُ اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ تَقَبَّلْ شَفَاعَتَهُ فِي أُمَّتِهِ وَ اِرْفَعْ دَرَجَتَهُ ثُمَّ تَحْمَدُ اَللَّهَ مَرَّتَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلاَثاً ثُمَّ تَقُومُ فَإِذَا جَلَسْتَ فِي اَلرَّابِعَةِ قُلْتَ بِسْمِ اَللَّهِ وَ بِاللَّهِ وَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ خَيْرُ اَلْأَسْمَاءِ لِلَّهِ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ أَرْسَلَهُ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيراً وَ نَذِيراً بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اَلسَّاعَةِ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّكَ نِعْمَ اَلرَّبُّ وَ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً نِعْمَ اَلرَّسُولُ اَلتَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ وَ اَلصَّلَوَاتُ اَلطَّاهِرَاتُ اَلطَّيِّبَاتُ اَلزَّاكِيَاتُ اَلْغَادِيَاتُ اَلرَّائِحَاتُ اَلسَّابِغَاتُ اَلنَّاعِمَاتُ لِلَّهِ مَا طَابَ وَ زَكَا وَ طَهُرَ وَ خَلَصَ وَ صَفَا فَلِلَّهِ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَرْسَلَهُ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيراً وَنَذِيراً بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اَلسَّاعَةِ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ رَبِّي نِعْمَ اَلرَّبُّ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّداً نِعْمَ اَلرَّسُولُ وَ أَشْهَدُ« أَنَّ اَلسّٰاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ لاٰ رَيْبَ فِيهٰا وَ أَنَّ اَللّٰهَ يَبْعَثُ مَنْ فِي اَلْقُبُورِ»« اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ اَلَّذِي هَدٰانٰا لِهٰذٰا وَ مٰا كُنّٰا لِنَهْتَدِيَ لَوْلاٰ أَنْ هَدٰانَا اَللّٰهُ»« اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ رَبِّ اَلْعٰالَمِينَ» اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَبَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ سَلِّمْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ تَرَحَّمْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ وَ بَارَكْتَ وَ تَرَحَّمْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ« اِغْفِرْ لَنٰا وَ لِإِخْوٰانِنَا اَلَّذِينَ سَبَقُونٰا بِالْإِيمٰانِ وَ لاٰ تَجْعَلْ فِي قُلُوبِنٰا غِلاًّ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا رَبَّنٰا إِنَّكَ رَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ» اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ اُمْنُنْ عَلَيَّ بِالْجَنَّةِ وَ عَافِنِي مِنَ اَلنَّارِ اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ اِغْفِرْ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ اَلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ« وَ لِمَنْ دَخَلَ بَيْتِيَ مُؤْمِناً وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَاَلْمُؤْمِنٰاتِ وَلاٰ تَزِدِ اَلظّٰالِمِينَ إِلاّٰ تَبٰاراً» ثُمَّ قُلِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا اَلنَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اَللَّهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَى أَنْبِيَاءِ اَللَّهِ وَ رُسُلِهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَى جَبْرَئِيلَ وَ مِيكَائِيلَ وَ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةِ اَلْمُقَرَّبِينَ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَى مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ خَاتَمِ اَلنَّبِيِّينَ لاَ نَبِيَّ بَعْدَهُ وَ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْنَا وَ عَلَى عِبَادِ اَللَّهِ اَلصَّالِحِينَ ثُمَّ تُسَلِّمُ»

items.e: Sa‘d ibn Abdillah, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah, who said: I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “What suffices to be said in the ‘tashahhud’ of the first two rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: “You say: ‘Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wahdahu la sharika lah’.” I said: “And what suffices in the ‘tashahhud’ of the last two rak‘ahs?” Imam (a.s) said: “The two testimonies.”
items.o: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَا يُجْزِي مِنَ اَلْقَوْلِ فِي اَلتَّشَهُّدِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ قَالَ« تَقُولُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ» قُلْتُ فَمَا يُجْزِي مِنْ تَشَهُّدِ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ« اَلشَّهَادَتَانِ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Hajjal, from Tha‘labah ibn Maymun, from Yahya ibn Talhah, from Sawrah ibn Kulayb, who said: I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the minimum that suffices for ‘tashahhud’. Imam (a.s) said: “The two testimonies (‘al-shahadatan’).”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ طَلْحَةَ عَنْ سَوْرَةَ بْنِ كُلَيْبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَدْنَى مَا يُجْزِي مِنَ اَلتَّشَهُّدِ قَالَ« اَلشَّهَادَتَانِ»

items.e: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sa‘d ibn Bakr, from Habib al-Khath‘ami: Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “If a man sits for the ‘tashahhud’ and praises Allah (swt), it suffices him.”
items.o: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ حَبِيبٍ اَلْخَثْعَمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِذَا جَلَسَ اَلرَّجُلُ لِلتَّشَهُّدِ فَحَمِدَ اَللَّهَ أَجْزَأَهُ»

items.e: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, the ‘tashahhud’ which is said in the second rak‘ah, is it sufficient if I say it in the fourth [rak‘ah] as well?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
items.o: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ اَلتَّشَهُّدُ اَلَّذِي فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ يُجْزِي أَنْ أَقُولَهُ فِي اَلرَّابِعَةِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»

items.e: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Bakr ibn Habib, who said: I asked Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the ‘tashahhud’. Imam (a.s) said: “If it were as they say, obligatory upon the people, they would have perished. Rather, the people used to say the simplest of what they knew. If you praise Allah (swt), it suffices you.”
items.o: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ عَنْ بَكْرِ بْنِ حَبِيبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلتَّشَهُّدِ فَقَالَ« لَوْ كَانَ كَمَا يَقُولُونَ وَاجِباً عَلَى اَلنَّاسِ هَلَكُوا إِنَّمَا كَانَ اَلْقَوْمُ يَقُولُونَ أَيْسَرَ مَا يَعْلَمُونَ إِذَا حَمِدْتَ اَللَّهَ أَجْزَأَكَ»

items.e: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “The ‘tashahhud’ in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “Twice.” I said: “And how is it said twice?” Imam (a.s) said: “When you sit upright, say: ‘Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wahdahu la sharika lah, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan Abduhu wa rasuluh,’ then you exit (complete the prayer).” I said: “What about the statement of the servant: ‘al-tahiyyatu lillah wa al-salawatu al-tayyibat lillah’?” Imam (a.s) said: “That is a graceful form of supplication, a kindness from the servant by which his Lord shows him grace.”
items.o: مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلتَّشَهُّدُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« مَرَّتَيْنِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ كَيْفَ مَرَّتَيْنِ قَالَ« إِذَا اِسْتَوَيْتَ جَالِساً فَقُلْ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ ثُمَّ تَنْصَرِفُ» قَالَ قُلْتُ قَوْلُ اَلْعَبْدِ اَلتَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ وَ اَلصَّلَوَاتُ اَلطَّيِّبَاتُ لِلَّهِ قَالَ« هَذَا اَللُّطْفُ مِنَ اَلدُّعَاءِ يَلْطُفُ اَلْعَبْدَ رَبُّهُ»

items.e: And from him, from Abu Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Ali, from ‘Ubayd, from Ya‘qub ibn Shu‘ayb: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “The ‘tashahhud’ in the book of (Imam) Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, is in two parts.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «اَلتَّشَهُّدُ فِي كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ شَفْعٌ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Bakr ibn Habib, who said: I said to Abu Ja‘far (a.s), peace be upon him: “What should I say in the ‘tashahhud’ and in the ‘qunut’?” Imam (a.s) said: “Say the best of what you know, for if it had been fixed (with strict wording), the people would have perished.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ عَنْ بَكْرِ بْنِ حَبِيبٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَيَّ شَيْءٍ أَقُولُ فِي اَلتَّشَهُّدِ وَ اَلْقُنُوتِ قَالَ« قُلْ بِأَحْسَنِ مَا عَلِمْتَ فَإِنَّهُ لَوْ كَانَ مُوَقَّتاً لَهَلَكَ اَلنَّاسُ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-‘Abbas, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from Hammad, from Abu Basir, who said: I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (a.s), and when He (a.s) reached the final ‘tashahhud’, He (a.s) raised his voice until we could hear him. When He (a.s) finished the prayer, I said to him: “Is it appropriate for the imam (of prayer) to make his ‘tashahhud’ audible to those behind him?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: صَلَّيْتُ خَلْفَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَلَمَّا كَانَ فِي آخِرِ تَشَهُّدِهِ رَفَعَ صَوْتَهُ حَتَّى أَسْمَعَنَا فَلَمَّا اِنْصَرَفَ قُلْتُ كَذَا يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُسْمِعَ تَشَهُّدَهُ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»

items.e: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman, from Abu Basir: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It is appropriate for the imam (of prayer) to make audible to those behind him everything that he says, and it is not appropriate for those behind the imam (of prayer) to make anything they say audible to him.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُسْمِعَ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ كُلَّمَا يَقُولُ وَلاَ يَنْبَغِي لِمَنْ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُسْمِعَهُ شَيْئاً مِمَّا يَقُولُ».

items.e: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “It is appropriate for the imam (of prayer) to make the ‘tashahhud’ audible to those behind him, and they should not make anything audible to him.”
